**Why:** Django stores applied migration records in a `django_migrations` database table with columns for app name, migration name, and application timestamp; the `MigrationRecorder` creates this table on-demand using the schema editor (avoiding the chicken-and-egg problem that migrations themselves can't be used to create it), and both the executor and loader interact with it to track which migrations have been applied to prevent re-running them.
